# Project Management Setup

This directory holds the *source of truth* for labels, milestones, and seed
issues. GitHub itself has no way to check these in declaratively (labels,
milestones, and Projects v2 boards all live in GitHub's own data, not the
repo tree), so we generate/maintain them here and push them out via scripts
in `../../scripts/`.

## Contents

- `labels.yml` — all repository labels with color and description
- `milestones.json` — the four roadmap milestones (v0.1 → v2.0), matching `ROADMAP.md`
- `issues.json` — 115 seed issues across every module, labeled by difficulty/area and mapped to a milestone. Generated by `scripts/generate_issues.py`; edit that script and regenerate rather than hand-editing the JSON, so the two stay in sync.

## One-time setup for a new GitHub repo

Run in this order (requires the [`gh` CLI](https://cli.github.com/), authenticated with repo admin access):

```bash
# 1. Labels
./scripts/setup-labels.sh <owner>/<repo>

# 2. Milestones
./scripts/setup-milestones.sh <owner>/<repo>

# 3. Seed issues (depends on labels + milestones existing)
./scripts/seed-issues.sh <owner>/<repo>

# 4. Project board (optional, needs `project` OAuth scope)
gh auth refresh -s project
./scripts/setup-project-board.sh <owner> <repo>
```

## Regenerating the issue set

Edit `scripts/generate_issues.py` (add/remove/edit issue entries), then:

```bash
python3 scripts/generate_issues.py
```

This overwrites `issues.json`. Re-running `seed-issues.sh` will create any
*new* issues but won't update or de-duplicate existing ones — GitHub has no
stable external ID to match against, so treat re-seeding as additive. If you
need to re-seed cleanly, close/delete the previously seeded issues first.

## Why not a single YAML per issue?

Some tools (e.g. `github-actions/issue-import`) support one-file-per-issue.
We chose a single JSON array instead because 115 issues as 115 separate files
is harder to review in a PR and harder to keep consistent (easy for one file
to drift from the label/milestone conventions the others follow). Revisit
this if the seed set needs to grow much further or needs per-issue review workflows.
